transcript.text: AEG IKB64301FB induction hob keeps beeping and showing Er03 then switches off. Pan of pasta boiled over just before.

I can’t confirm an exact meaning for ER03 on this AEG hob from the code alone, so I would not treat it as a confirmed component fault. Given that pasta boiled over immediately beforehand, moisture around the touch controls, or having tracked under the edge of the glass, is the most likely cause of the beeping and switch-off. 1. Switch the hob off at its isolator/fused spur and leave it isolated. When cool, remove all pans and thoroughly dry the whole glass, especially the control strip and around the glass edges. Do not pour cleaner or water into the edges.
2. Leave it to dry properly before retrying — ideally several hours, longer if a lot of liquid spilled. This allows any moisture affecting the touch controls to evaporate.
3. When you restore power, test it with the surface dry, no pan on it, and nothing resting over the controls. If it now behaves normally, the spill was the cause. If ER03 returns straight away once it is completely dry, or it reappears during use without another spill, the more likely possibilities are a touch-control/control-board issue or overheating/cooling fault. Those are engineer jobs on an induction hob; don’t remove the underside or attempt internal checks. If there is any burning smell, scorching, or it trips the electrics, leave it isolated and arrange service.

Ok, I wiped it dry and switched it off at the wall for 5 minutes. It works now, all four zones. A wooden spoon was resting on the edge of the controls too, so I moved that. No burning smell and no cracks in the glass.

That points strongly to the boil-over moisture and/or the spoon interfering with the touch-control area, rather than an internal hob fault. As all four zones are now working and there is no burning smell or glass damage, it is fine to continue using it. Keep the control strip clear and dry, particularly after a pan boils over. If ER03 returns when the surface is fully dry and nothing is touching the controls, leave the hob off and arrange an engineer, as that would suggest a touch-control or internal control fault. Is there anything else with the hob or another appliance you would like help with?

candidates: Moisture on or beneath the touch-control area after the boil-over (high)
Touch-control or control-board fault if it persists when completely dry (low)

reading.symptom: Keeps beeping, shows Er03, then switches off

plan: Already given by the customer, never ask for it again: make AEG; model IKB64301FB; code ER03.
The fault they reported is: "Keeps beeping, shows Er03, then switches off". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the safe checks that best tell those causes apart (most useful and simplest first, usually two to four), each with why it helps and what each result would mean; or, if one question would settle it sooner, ask that. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.

Explain what the error code means using ERROR CODES. If ERROR CODES does not resolve it, say plainly that you cannot confirm what it means on their model (it may not be an error code at all, for example part of the model name), never guess a meaning, and work from the symptoms.

candidates: Moisture or an object on the touch-control area after the boil-over (high)
plan: The customer says it is fixed: say so warmly, give one short tip to stop it happening again, and ask if there is anything else.

facts.value: Wiped the hob dry: It works now, all four zones
